subject: math.MP
name: Yang–Mills existence and mass gap
statement: For each compact simple gauge group, construct a nontrivial quantum Yang–Mills theory on R^4 satisfying the standard rigorous axioms and prove that its Hamiltonian has a strictly positive mass gap above the vacuum.
importance: It would place a fundamental theory of particle interactions on a rigorous mathematical foundation.
status_note: The Clay problem concerns continuum four-dimensional quantum Yang–Mills theory; lattice and lower-dimensional results do not settle it.

references.title: Yang–Mills and Mass Gap, Clay Mathematics Institute

subject: math.MP
name: Three-dimensional Navier–Stokes regularity
statement: For every smooth divergence-free initial velocity on R^3 with finite energy and sufficient decay, does the incompressible Navier–Stokes equation with positive viscosity and no external force have a smooth solution for all positive times?
importance: It asks whether the standard equations of viscous fluids can create singularities from smooth data.
status_note: Global weak solutions exist; smooth global existence in two dimensions does not settle the three-dimensional problem.

subject: math.MP
name: Weak cosmic censorship for asymptotically flat vacuum gravity
statement: For generic smooth asymptotically flat initial data for the Einstein vacuum equations, is future null infinity complete, so singularities formed by gravitational collapse are not visible to distant observers?
importance: It tests whether classical gravitational evolution preserves predictability for external observers.
status_note: Genericity and suitable asymptotic conditions are essential; exceptional naked singularities and results in symmetric matter models do not settle the general vacuum question.

subject: math.MP
name: Strong cosmic censorship for asymptotically flat vacuum gravity
statement: For generic smooth asymptotically flat vacuum initial data, is the maximal globally hyperbolic spacetime development inextendible as a Lorentzian manifold with a C^2 metric?
importance: It asks whether generic Einstein evolution has a unique maximal future governed by the initial data.
status_note: The extension regularity is part of the conjecture; other matter models, a positive cosmological constant, and weaker regularity can yield different formulations and answers.

subject: math.MP
name: Nonlinear stability of all subextremal Kerr black holes
statement: Do sufficiently small smooth asymptotically flat vacuum perturbations of every Kerr exterior with |a| less than M remain globally regular outside the black hole and settle toward another Kerr exterior?
importance: It would justify rotating black holes as stable endpoints of gravitational evolution.
status_note: Nonlinear stability is established for slowly rotating regimes; the full subextremal rotation range is open. Extremal |a| = M is excluded.

subject: math.MP
name: Conformal scaling limit of the three-dimensional critical Ising model
statement: Prove existence, universality, and conformal invariance of a nontrivial continuum scaling limit of the nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Ising model on Z^3 at its critical temperature.
importance: It would rigorously explain the universal continuum theory of a major three-dimensional phase transition.
status_note: Two-dimensional critical Ising theory is understood much more fully; numerical conformal-bootstrap predictions and partial three-dimensional results do not constitute this theorem.

subject: math.MP
name: Area law for gapped quantum systems in two dimensions
statement: Must the entanglement entropy of a simply connected region be bounded by a constant times its boundary size in the unique ground state of every two-dimensional finite-range local quantum Hamiltonian with bounded local dimension, uniformly bounded interaction strength, and a uniform spectral gap?
importance: It would explain why low-energy quantum matter can often be represented efficiently by tensor networks.
status_note: One-dimensional area laws are proved; the general interacting two-dimensional statement with a uniform gap and unique ground state remains open.

references.title: Area laws for the entanglement entropy – a review

subject: math.MP
name: Bose–Einstein condensation in an interacting continuum gas
statement: Prove Bose–Einstein condensation, expressed by off-diagonal long-range order, at sufficiently low positive temperature for a homogeneous three-dimensional continuum Bose gas with a nonzero repulsive finite-range two-body interaction in the thermodynamic limit.
importance: It asks for a rigorous foundation of a central quantum phase of interacting matter.
status_note: The ideal gas, some lattice or mean-field models, and trapped scaling limits are understood; they do not establish this interacting homogeneous thermodynamic-limit statement.

references.title: The Mathematics of the Bose Gas and its Condensation

subject: math.MP
name: Delocalization in the three-dimensional Anderson model
statement: For the nearest-neighbor Anderson Hamiltonian on Z^3 with sufficiently weak independent identically distributed bounded random on-site potential, prove an interval of absolutely continuous spectrum in the interior of the unperturbed band.
importance: It would rigorously establish the metallic side of the disorder-driven localization transition.
status_note: Localization is proved in several regimes; absolutely continuous spectrum on tree graphs does not settle the cubic-lattice problem.

subject: math.MP
name: Confinement in continuum four-dimensional Yang–Mills theory
statement: For four-dimensional pure SU(3) quantum Yang–Mills theory, rigorously establish confinement through a positive asymptotic string tension, meaning an area law for sufficiently large fundamental Wilson loops after suitable renormalization.
importance: It would explain mathematically why isolated color charges are not observed.
status_note: The continuum theory must first be constructed; strong-coupling lattice results and a mass gap alone do not prove continuum confinement.
